title: How do you personalize direct mail by generation?
summary: Personalization drives direct mail conversions, but what feels relevant changes by generation. Here's what the data says and how to put it into practice for each audience.
body_markdown:
Personalization drives direct mail performance. According to Lob's[State of Direct Mail Consumer Insights 2026](https://www.lob.com/state-of-direct-mail/consumer-insights/2026-report) ** report, **89% of consumers say relevant mail is what influences them to take action** .


But relevance looks different depending on who's holding the piece. The offer, the message, and even the format that resonates with a Gen Z consumer could miss with a Boomer, and vice versa.


## Gen Z: identity, life stage, and brand credibility


Gen Z[responds strongly to personalization](https://www.lob.com/blog/how-can-i-enhance-personalization-in-my-direct-mail-pieces-beyond-basic-name-fields) that reflects who they are and where they are in life. The report found that Gen Z is more than twice as likely as Boomers to respond to life-stage personalization.


They also care about brand credibility in a way older generations don't as strongly. **55% of Gen Z say receiving direct mail from a brand makes it feel more credible** , and 59% say it feels special. For a generation that grew up in a digital-first world, a physical piece signals that a brand made a deliberate effort to reach them.


QR codes work well with this audience too. And 44% of Gen Z enrolled in Informed Delivery click promotion links often, the highest of any generation.


## Millennials: relevance, timing, and digital integration


Millennials are more likely to convert from direct mail than any other generation. **75% have made a purchase, signed up for a service, or become a customer as a result of receiving a piece** .


What moves them is relevance tied to something they're actively considering, combined with an easy path to act digitally. 52% of Millennials say direct mail feels more trustworthy than digital communication, the highest of any generation.


They also share mail at high rates, which means a well-targeted piece can travel beyond the original recipient.


## Boomers: offers, discounts, and familiarity


Unlike younger generations, boomers are driven almost entirely by offers and discounts. **62% say including an offer or discount influenced them to take action** .


They're also the most likely to prefer a letter in an envelope format, and the least likely to engage with QR codes or digital response paths.


For Boomers, personalization means relevance to a current need and a clear, credible offer. Life stage messaging and name-level personalization matter less than practical value.


## How to put it into action


No matter the generation, personalized mail converts. Technical bottlenecks shouldn’t stop you from sending it. Look for no-code tools, like[Lob’s No-Code Design Suite](https://www.lob.com/no-code) , that help you and your team build dynamic templates, swap offers and imagery by segment, and get campaigns into production[without relying on developers](https://www.lob.com/blog/how-do-you-scale-direct-mail-personalization-without-a-developer) .
